title: Adaptive Experimentation Lab Protocol and Metric Harmonization
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document defines the Adaptive Experimentation Lab Protocol (AELP) used by the serving runtime team to design, run, and interpret experiments that touch kernel scheduling, KV cache behavior, quantization policy, and end-to-end request fidelity. It also standardizes metric names and harmonizes telemetry so experiment results are comparable across benchmarking suites and release gates.

Goal:
- Shorten time to actionable insight for runtime tuning changes while preserving safety for production systems.
- Produce repeatable experiment artifacts that feed the benchmarking suite and the release regression gates.
- Provide a clear triage/runbook path for experiments that regress SLOs or increase cost beyond thresholds.

Scope:
- Applies to all kernel-level changes, scheduler policy experiments, runtime-level sampling/telemetry changes, and quantization rollouts that will be evaluated against the platform SLOs (p95 latency, p99 latency, correctness fuzzing score, and per-token cost).
- Not intended for model architecture research or user-space application logic experiments.

Key definitions (metric harmonization):
- request.p95_latency_ms: 95th percentile end-to-end request latency measured at the ingress proxy (ms).
- request.p99_latency_ms: 99th percentile latency at ingress (ms).
- kernel.exec_time_ms: median kernel execution time per token (ms) measured at GPU-side tracepoints.
- kvcache.hit_rate_percent: KV cache hit rate measured over session lifecycle (%).
- fidelity.regression_score: A weighted score (0-100) computed by the evaluation harness comparing generated outputs against golden prompt sets. Lower is better (0 = no regression).
- cost.per_token_usd: accounting-backed cost per token for the experiment cohort (USD/token).
- sla_violation_count: number of requests that missed the configured SLO target.

Experiment roles and ownership:
- Experiment Lead: owns hypothesis, design, and run completion (typically feature owner).
- Lab Operator: prepares infra, dataset, and traffic shaping; coordinates with infra/SRE for capacity.
- Telemetry Owner: ensures traces, spans, and custom metrics are instrumented and names conform to harmonized schema.
- Reviewer(s): runs result review and signs off before progressing experiment to canary or rollout.

Experiment lifecycle (AELP steps):
1) Hypothesis & Acceptance Criteria (doc):
   - State the precise hypothesis in one sentence. Example: "AdaptiveBatcher reduces median kernel.exec_time_ms by >= 10% for short-sequence workloads without increasing request.p99_latency_ms by > 3%".
   - Define pass/fail: metrics and thresholds (p95/p99 latency, fidelity.regression_score delta, cost delta).
2) Safety Constraints & Blast Radius Plan:
   - Minimum traffic and cohort isolation requirements.
   - Automatic abort thresholds (see Thresholds table below).
3) Infra & Dataset Setup:
   - Provide a config (YAML) that can be replayed by the benchmarking harness.
   - Reserve test GPU pool or use dedicated experiment nodes.
4) Observability Checklist:
   - Ensure traces capture kernel_id, batch_size, sequence_length, kvcache_lookup_count.
   - Ensure metrics are emitted to telemetry namespace: runtime.lab.<metric>.
5) Dry-run (lab sandbox):
   - Run synthetic traffic at 10% of target load with request surface replay. Validate telemetry cardinality and sample rates.
6) Canary run (shadow and limited traffic):
   - Run at up to 1% production-equivalent traffic using traffic mirroring; do not route user traffic.
   - If canary passes acceptance criteria, schedule full canary where up to 5% of traffic is routed.
7) Full rollout planning and rollout policy document with rollback criteria.

Thresholds and Automated Abort Rules:
- abort.on_p99_increase_pct = 5% (if request.p99_latency_ms increases by more than 5% vs baseline, abort).
- abort.on_fidelity_regression_score_delta = 2 (if fidelity.regression_score increases by >= 2 points, abort).
- abort.on_cost_increase_pct = 10% (if cost.per_token_usd increases by >10%, abort unless business ok).
- abort.on_sla_violations = 50/min (if sla_violation_count exceeds 50/minute, abort).

Telemetry contract (plain-text table):
- Column headers: metric_name | description | required_tags | sample_rate
- runtime.lab.request.p95_latency_ms | E2E p95 at ingress | route,model_variant,cohort | 1.0
- runtime.lab.kernel.exec_time_ms | kernel execution time per token | kernel_id,batch_size,sequence_length | 0.1
- runtime.lab.kvcache.hit_rate_percent | KV cache hit ratio per session | session_id,model_variant | 0.5
- runtime.lab.fidelity.regression_score | Eval harness regression measure | prompt_set_id,experiment_id | 1.0

Experiment config example (YAML snippet):
---
experiment_id: adaptive-batcher-2026-11
description: Test adaptive batcher heuristics for short sequences
traffic: replayed-corpus: small-seq-corpus-v2
cohorts:
  - name: control
    nodes: t2-experiment-pool
    route_weight: 50
  - name: variant
    nodes: t2-experiment-pool
    route_weight: 50
metrics:
  - name: runtime.lab.request.p95_latency_ms
    aggregation: percentile(95)
  - name: runtime.lab.kernel.exec_time_ms
    aggregation: median
abort_rules:
  - metric: runtime.lab.request.p99_latency_ms
    threshold: 1.05 baseline
    action: abort
  - metric: runtime.lab.fidelity.regression_score
    threshold: +2
    action: abort
---

Benchmarking suite integration:
- Every experiment must produce a tarball: {experiment_id}_artifacts.tar.gz containing: replay config, traces (sampled), aggregated metrics JSON, and evaluation harness results.
- The benchmark runner ingests the tarball and runs post-processing to produce standardized CSVs used by release gates.
- Hooks are provided to register the experiment run with the SLO regression tracker (CI job: ci/benchmarks/register-experiment).

Kernel scheduling experiment guidelines:
- For scheduler policy changes, include microbenchmarks that exercise batch slicing, preemption, and cooperative handoff.
- Recommended microbenchmarks: single-token microburst, mixed-concurrency 1:10 short:long sequences, preemption stress with 80% slot occupancy.
- Collect per-kernel per-core occupancy heatmaps and summarize as occupancy_percentiles (p50/p90/p99).

Runbook: if experiment triggers automated abort or incident:
1) Pause all experiment cohorts and set route_weight=0 for variant nodes.
2) Capture minimal reproduction trace: run synthetic replay at 10% load with full sampling.
3) Run quick-check scripts:
   - scripts/telemetry/check_slo_deltas.sh --experiment $ID
   - scripts/runtime/collect-hotpath.sh --since 10m --experiment $ID
4) Escalation: page oncall@redwood with subject "AELP abort: <experiment_id>" and include the baseline vs variant deltas snapshot.
5) If kernel-level regression suspected, open a kernel-ticket and attach sampled PTX/trace and the kernel.exec_time_ms distribution.
6) If no root cause within 4 hours, revert the scheduler change and schedule a retro.

Release note fragment (for changes that graduate from AELP):
- Version: runtime 3.8.0-experiment.
- Summary: AdaptiveBatcher reduces median kernel.exec_time_ms by 12% for short sequences; no p99 regression observed in 7-day canary.
- Risk: Minor increase in memory churn observed under extreme mixed workloads (p99 memory alloc rate +6%). See known issues entry K-2026-71.

Known issues observed during lab experiments (K- prefixes):
- K-2025-33: Telemetry cardinality explosion when sequence_length tag is left unbounded; mitigation: cap sequence_length buckets to {1,8,64,256,1024}.
- K-2026-71: Memory churn spike under mixed long/short cohorts when adaptive batching interacts with preemption; mitigation: scheduler backoff and reduced slice size.
- K-2026-99: Intermittent fidelity.regression_score spikes correlated with quantization profile 8-bit +/- aggressive weight folding.

Appendix A: Safe-checklist before canary rollout:
- [ ] Telemetry emitted and visible in dashboards (dashboard: Lab/Experiments/<experiment_id>).
- [ ] Automated abort rules configured in experiment config and tested.
- [ ] Infra operator signed off on GPU pool reservation.
- [ ] Rollback owner and communications plan documented.

Appendix B: Useful CLI commands:
- Mirror traffic to experiment canary (dry-run):
  redwood traffic mirror --from route=prod --to experiment=adaptive-batcher-2026-11 --sample-rate=0.01
- Register experiment artifacts with CI:
  ci/benchmarks/register-experiment --id adaptive-batcher-2026-11 --artifacts ./adaptive-batcher-2026-11_artifacts.tar.gz
